Topics · Is there a God?

Why would a perfect being need worship?

It would not: the need runs the other way, the argument says. Why create at all has no complete answer.

Part 1 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

Quran · Fatir 35:15

Translation

The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·

Acts · 17:24-25

World English Bible

Your objection is sound. A being that lacks nothing cannot need praise. If worship fills a gap in God, the picture is of a vain king, and the argument against him wins. So test the claim as stated. This verse agrees with your premise and goes further: it says that He is the one with no need, and that the needy ones are us. Whatever worship is, it cannot be something God is short of. So the question has to change.

A question for you

If worship does not meet a need in God, what could it be?

If you saySomething pointless.
ThenThat is possible. It deserves examination before you adopt it, which comes next.
If you saySomething that benefits the worshipper.
ThenThat is where the next argument goes. It has to show how.
If you sayA tool for controlling people.
ThenSome have used it that way, and no one here denies it. That use does not explain all of it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Their meat will not reach Allāh, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may glorify Allāh for that [to] which He has guided you; and give good tidings to the doers of good.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:37

Translation

If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it. Will I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving. Pay your vows to the Most High.

Original · Hebrew

אִם־אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃ הַֽ֭אוֹכַל בְּשַׂ֣ר אַבִּירִ֑ים וְדַ֖ם עַתּוּדִ֣ים אֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃ זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה וְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְעֶלְי֣וֹן נְדָרֶֽיךָ׃

the Psalms · 50:12-14

World English Bible

Take the plainest case: sacrifice. Surely that is feeding a god. This verse denies it in the bluntest terms: neither its flesh nor its blood reaches God. What reaches Him is the person's own awareness. So the act is doing something on the human side. Compare saying thank you. A generous person does not need it. Yet someone who never says it is becoming a certain kind of person. Worship is claimed to work like that: it shapes the one who does it.

A question for you

How far does this explanation go for you?

If you sayIt explains worship, but not being commanded to it.
ThenThat is the stronger objection: why would it be a duty? The next part takes it up.
If you sayA person can get that without God.
ThenMany reach some of it. The claim here is larger: that there is really someone to thank.
If you sayI did not find this in my experience.
ThenThat matters, and it is not denied here. Forced worship is often emptied of all this.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ٥٦ مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ٥٧ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ٥٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider,[1548] the firm possessor of strength.

Translator's notes

[1548] Providing everything required by His creations during their decreed existence. His provision includes guidance.

Quran · Adh-Dhariyat 51:56-58

Translation

If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it.

Original · Hebrew

אִם־אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃

the Psalms · 50:12

World English Bible

Now the hard sentence: creation is said to be for worship. Read the next two lines. No provision is wanted from anyone; no feeding is wanted. So it is not a transaction. Then why create at all? The honest answer: the text says for what, not why He would want it, and no complete answer is known. Classical thinkers spoke of generosity overflowing, and critics will find that thin. What can be said is narrower. Being oriented to what is true is held to be a human good.

A question for you

Where does the question stop for you?

If you sayWhy create at all?
ThenThe answer stops there too. No complete answer is known.
If you sayWhy is anyone punished for not worshipping?
ThenThat is a serious question, and this does not answer it. It has its own places.
If you sayWhat do I do with this?
ThenNothing is required. For anyone who wants it, there is a short page on speaking to Him.

The same in the other books

Translation

This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.

Original · Hebrew

ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־זֶ֖ה כָּל־הָאָדָֽם׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:13

World English Bible

Translation

For you don’t delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה ע֝וֹלָ֗ה לֹ֣א תִרְצֶֽה׃ זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֪וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃

the Psalms · 51:16-17

World English Bible

Translation

But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.

Original · Ancient Greek

εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:7

World English Bible

Translation

Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.

Original · Hebrew

וְקִרְע֤וּ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַל־בִּגְדֵיכֶ֔ם וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ ה֔וּא אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃

Joel · 2:13

World English Bible
